title: Claude Monet's birth chart
metaDescription: Claude Monet's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 22.2° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.1° separates Mars and Saturn from an exact square; at that range drive and structure read as one mechanism. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 22.2° Scorpio, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is the Moon. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 14.6° Sagittarius, Venus was at 21.2° Sagittarius, Mars was at 20.4° Virgo. Read together: thought that arrives already in motion; attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Mars square Saturn, 0.1° of separation. Right angles are where the scheme puts its grit. A square asks two functions to work in a mode neither would have chosen. Behind it, Venus conjunction Saturn at 0.7°, and Venus square Mars at 0.8° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Mars opposes Uranus while both square Mercury. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags a single placement in this chart. Mercury in Sagittarius at 14.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 4 fire, 3 water, 1 earth, 1 air by element and 5 mutable, 3 fixed, 1 cardinal by mode. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.3° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
